# Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models run one block of layers several times per token and, at inference, run the
> same number of loops to prefill the prompt and to decode each answer token. This work unties the two with a small
> loop adapter (LoRA + per-loop RoPE-commuting KV maps on a frozen model; one set of parameters for all 16 pairs of
> prefill loops m and decode loops n up to four) and measures what each count buys on Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B,
> Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview and Lev looped decision models. The paper's statistics
> are recomputed from released per-item scores by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py.

Main findings (95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper):
- The best prefill count depends on the benchmark, its prompt and the decode budget (task map over 16 (m, n) pairs on 13
  benchmark settings, Ouro-2.6B). Within one adapter, 4-shot MATH-500 with one prefill loop instead of four: 51.8 -> 68.4 at four
  decode loops; MMLU needs three or four prefill loops.
- Choosing m per benchmark on held-out halves beats native Ouro-2.6B with the same number of decode loops significantly
  on 11 of 13 settings with one decode loop (+5 to +21) and 9 of 13 with two (selection-aware intervals); against the
  same adapter's n/n: 6 and 3 of 13; mixed with three or four. Ouro-1.4B (13 settings): 10 and 2 of 13.
- Ouro-2.6B-Thinking: prefill 4 / decode 2 above native 2/2 on eight benchmarks (significant on five) and above a LoRA
  distillation of native 2/2 with the same data and teacher (MMLU-Pro +5.2, ARC-C +2.9); 0.55x the answer time of native 4/4
  on 64 timed GSM8K problems.
- Lev looped decision models, both directions: more prefill than decision loops is significantly above a matched
  control on 12 of 13 (m, n) pairs (+4.4 to +7.5 at one decision loop); fewer is below it on all 13 (significantly 11).
- One stored prompt KV cache serves every decode loop exactly (RoPE-commuting key scale applied to the query).

Limitations stated by the author: the prefill count is calibrated per benchmark, not routed per prompt; the best count
depends on prompt format and checkpoint; with three or four decode loops native models are better on long-context
retrieval; comparisons with native models include adapter training; equal decode loops do not mean equal latency.

## Docs
- README.md: findings, when to use, repository map
- REPRODUCE.md: every table and figure -> script -> result file; training and evaluation commands
- paper/untying-prefill-decode-loops.pdf: the paper
- ouro/results/items/: per-item scores of every run the paper uses; ouro/results/paper_numbers.json: the recomputed statistics
